reviews.review_msg: Professor Emrul is a great lecturer. His classes are clear and entertaining, and his tests are fair. He is very supportive in both academic and professional settings and always willing to help during his office hours. I'd recommend that anyone take his courses.

Great prof! Very caring and is straight up. Wants students to succeed and knows the right way to do so. Studied a lot himself so he has all the tips and tricks up his sleeve for success that you will need - talk to him!

I took this course in UBC 2019 W, and he was the best ECON prof I have ever met. His lectures were most engaging and I certainly learned a lot. I aced it with grade of 94. Even in my internships the trade models are of great help for me to have a better understanding of why my senior managers can make such decisions. I strongly recommend it!

The exams are hard and his last exam was on the last day of class. But he really cares about his students and put in the effort to help them. This is what I love about him. He gives options to improve our overall grade by offering different weight transfers, so I think he is fair.

Professor Hasan is the professor that I truly admire. Besides his caring for student mental health, great willingness to give career advice, His class is full of joy and wisdom. Highly recommend taking his Econ355 at UBC; learning International trade models and policy tools gives you a great advantage in doing Macro-analysis as an Econ student.

Great ProfTook both his ECON383 and ECON355w. Although there is a lot content in the lectures, you can get good grade if you listen carefully in his class and do enough practices. I like his teaching style, always teach us by using real life examples-show us the bank website to find things that correlated with concepts.
He is a really good prof. I like his teaching style, and it's easy to get a good grade.
I like his enthusiasm for econ. He discusses trade theory with easy examples from real world that helps me to remember the outcomes.
He is new to UBC but he is a great teacher. Our class is only 50 minutes long each day so he kind of has to rush in more classes but he explains the concepts well. I will recommend him highly.
You need to self study in this class, otherwise it's difficult to learn
polite and kind, hard-working on helping you
Good prof!
Amazing Lectures
I really like his teaching style!!!!! I would like to take his other course again!!!!

He is a really good prof who tried to help everyone in his class. If you get in trouble with the assignments or midterms(I hope not), then you should attend every tutorial to get extra bonus marks. If this is your last class, then you'd better let him know it, since he is very kind to his students. In short, he is a professional and helpful prof.
The course is quite straightforward as Emrul does not test much math, it is simply equations of some economic models other than that its just reading, you get it you do well.
He is a nice professor! I really like his course. If you study hard, you will get really good grade!
Very passionate instructor and he works very hard to make sure students understand the concepts. Available outside class too.

Amazing prof and class!! After taking this class I realized that I wanted to specialize in economic development! I have never loved an econ this much before! There's a few writing assignments which are fair, and the midterm and final are fair.
Emurl teaches really well. I like his teaching style very much. The phenomenon in class is easygoing but we have never missed any important point.

Econ355w had so much take-home and in-class assignments. The work was heavy but the instructor's dedication towards academic honesty is amazing. He made some assignments in-class so that students cannot hire outside people to write the assignment for them. I liked it. 5 star for that :)

He is an awesome pro, always use his own examples to help us understand materials. Always finish class early and expect us to read. He gave the assignments not only for testing but also for helping us learning class. Definitely will take him again

His lectures were interesting as he tried to incorporate personal experiences to make the concepts more memorable (which did work). The assignments were relatively easy (600 words), but TH questions were TOUGH. Only had a final (45%) which was fair if you followed along with tutorial questions and assignment Qs.

I'm glad I got to take a class with Emrul. He's a good lecturer and adds a great amount of perspective to the base content of the class. The lectures can be a bit dry, but Emrul has a good sense of humour. He's very clear on what you should study, he drops hints every week as for what could end up on the final.

Thank you Emrul. One of the most influential lecturers I've ever had, thanks to him my political and economic views are more eclectic. I thoroughly enjoyed the class with him and I hope he continues to teach.

He replies emails really fast and very efficient at solving problem. He is hilarious and nice. His exam is fair if you do all the work by yourself (don't cheat) and attend lectures and tutorials. If you feel like you are failing the course, just try your best on exam and you will always be surprised by the mark you receive.

This class is not hard, just tried to finish all assignments by urself and reading lectures. This prof is Fair, and he really hates cheating, but he's nice and still give some cheating students marks... i think final exam is esay if u work by urself...

Professor Emrul had a defined structure for the course, was clear about expectations and readings, and his comments/suggestions for those who attended the lectures was really helpful for midterm and finals preparation. His grading criteria for the short papers were concise and helps to learn outside the textbook via research. Good professor!

I really enjoyed this class it was my nest mark in university. This teacher was very helpful and very passionate about his work. He was very fair and I learned a lot. I would definitely take this class again.
What a prof!!! So amazed!! Love him :)
the best prof I have ever had, really good man
As long as you read stuff on text book, and write notes during lectures, you will get what you deserve.
he is a very helpful peofessor
One of the simplest classes, made lectures interesting with examples. Would take a class with him again, if possible.
good professor , nobody can fail
Best professor ever. Didn't fail any students in his class this semester if you do all the exams and assignments. 5 assignments and only 600 words each. Should take 355 with him!
He is a excellent prof. the lecture was really useful and just attend his lecture and tutorial, you will be more than fine.
excellent professor.

the class is a breeze i never showed up and ended up with a B+, the exams are fair the final was a bit more challenging than the midterm but not impossible. The only bad thing about the class was the TA favoured some students over others and this was a bit annoying but the class was interesting and easy and Alex was a clear prof

Really great professor. Notes are clear and explains concepts really well so that you don't even need to read the book. Assignments are relatively interesting and aren't too difficult. Midterm and Final's are fair but the quantitative parts involving math are definitely challenging and tricky.

I got 95% in the quizzes... and something like 50% for the weekly op-eds. Completely nonsense criteria for grading them, no consistency week to week. It seemed like TAs would flip a coin whether an op-ed would pass, one week I pass, one week I don't, one week I pass, one week I don't... Better than my friend who never passed a single one I guess.
do not take his course, unfair to grade assignments!!

Chris is one of the best professors in the Econ department. The course was graded on weekly quizzes (40%) which were pretty difficult most weeks. The course also has weekly writing assignments (30%) which are easy if you're a good writer. 20% of the grade is a major writing assignment...don't worry its short and similar to the weekly assignments.

Honestly, very knowledgeable and one of the best communicators I've ever met. Absolutely take the course! The marking was very fair and Chris gives great feedback! Also encourages creative questions! The only con to the course was the tutorials, which were exceedingly painful because of the entire lack of English proficiency by the student body.
Heavy weight on online weekly quizzes which are hard af.
Avoid Him....
ECON 355 W is hard. The class average is super low.
not the sharpest knife in the drawer
Nice Prof but NOT ENOUGH TIME for the exam. (or too long exam in a short period)

Just becareful not to get too cocky with this class. It's totally possible to to get 100% leading up to the final exam however due to the nature of downward scaling and the easiness of the class, you'll probably end up with a C to a B if you walked in with a perfect mark. I personally didn't enjoy myself too much here.
Nice prof.  He likes to ask students to sit right in front him especially when they come in late. Easy to get high grade.
I'm in my final year and he is easily the best teacher I've had.
he deserves a :)
one of the best, most interesting, humorous econ prof.

He is a really good teacher. His teaching style is more holistic than most SFU course. You learn a great deal that is directly applicable to the real world economy. Lectures were always interesting, we even have class debates. Final was long and you can't memorize for the final, you got to understand the economy condition (past/current).

His lectures are pretty interesting because he uses a lot of examples. However..he tends to go off topic. But overall, his exams are pretty easy...just as long as you follow the hints that he gives out during lectures.
A professor with an excellent sense of humour and a pleasant demeanor.  He enjoys speaking with his students and goes to great lengths to explain the material.
No Comments
to be fair, the prof. is pretty good, but hard exam~ also, bad TA - Bryan Yu
interesting and funny but don't caught eating or sleeping
to be fair, his exam is not that hard, but i have to say that the multiple chioce part is tooooo tricky, and the time for exam is not enough. though the class is fun, however, not very useful.
No Comments
One of the best profs in econ. Great story teller, and is extremely knowledgable. Very funny guy who swears quite a bit.
Very good class, highly knowledgable prof, entertaining, easy exams, what more could you ask for?  Listen when he mumbles.. that is what is on the exams.  Easy A
Absolutely the worse professor at SFU.  Beware, he takes pictures of his students during lecture...
Zzzzz~~~

He's the worse prof that i've ever had.  He constantly mumbles when he's talking about important points that he will put on a test.  When I went to see him, he was no clearer.  His graphs are unclear.
Great Stories, most entertaining econ prof ever.  And he wears the sunglasses cause he's got a medical condition with his eyes, but hard to figure out what he wants on the exams, just study it all!

Very enjoyable class... keep up in the reading and pay attention to his main topics... very enjoyable lectures... but it's up to you to get the point out of it. If he offers extra ciricular activities take them... they're great opportunities! good course
He takes the class outside of economics to look at the big picture, which I found to be great
Lazy prof who always wear old-fashioned sunglasses to classes. His lectures were boring and I didn't learn much from this course~ As a recommendation, DON T take econ 355 with him!
haha..why would someone wear sun glasses in lecture hall?
No Comments
Funny lectures....try to get an easy TA cause Devoretz doesn't mark anything.
The most unorganized prof i know, he expects you to know things he doesn't teach
haha entertaining lectures
Lectures are a hell-of-a-lotta fun! Funny anecdotes keep lectures interesting

THIS PROFESSOR IS AMAZING. I have no clue why others keep giving him bad grade. He's super nice and very helpful. Worth taking a course with him for sure! If you cannot survive his class you should not be able to call yourself an economics major. He's very easy and very very good!

He is very nice and helpful, if you go to his office, he will be always help you, although the assignments are too difficult,the exams are easier, if you study all the assignments, tutorial question and lecture notes, it would be fine.

so regard taking with him! He talked too fast during lecture and feels like he is giving lecture to students who do well in the class. When I tried to ask question after class, I confused even more after and he kept saying 'it's all in the note/text'; wtx would I need a instructor if I can fully understand the material by myself...

Materials aren't that hard but he makes things so much harder by using very unreasonable teaching method. Assignments instructions are confusing as hell but he expects students to answer them perfectly just in 200-300 words.
WOW....

Instead of teaching actual material in the course, this power trip spends time plotting way in which to punish students.  The material he does teach is a bunch of formulas with no explanation as to how it relates into developmental economics.

I recommend taking all of your classes with Georgi.  He is a great professor and is not on a power trip at all.  His exams are so easy you can write them with your eyes closed.   This course and professor are definitely a GPA booster.  Best of all, if you miss a class you can teach yourself the material using the $200 textbook he demands you buy.
lecture notes are very disorganized and confusing. The assignments are even worse however graded very strictly
Georgi's lecture notes are pretty straightforward.  Write everything down and do the tutorial assignments, and it all makes sense.  The written assignments take a long time, but this is a W class.
His lecture notes are disorganized and the lecture itself is very confusing. The assignments are even worse however graded very strictly
very confusing lecture,notes are disorganized. assignemnts are even worse and very strictly graded.

Believe you me, stay away from this prof. First he gives a bunch of textbook recommendations, then after people buy them, decides not to use them. You have nothing to fall back on because his teaching abilities are so poor , he tries to punish his students. Makes mistakes all the time, thinks he knows what he's doing but he really doesn't.

I already took two semesters with him, and he is an amazing professor! You will learn more if you go to his office hours and his lectures are easy to understand with real life examples. The only thing I was complaining was TAs are not very good...
The professor has truly been my favourite Econ professor at SFU. Lectures are kind of boring but his exams are very much the same material he teaches.

This professor does not go through the necessary materials required for the exams. I get it, teaching the same thing every day might be boring but it is no excuse to rush everything. We wanna go home too but we paid thousands of dollars here to study. Wish he put more time and effort. The material itself is not super difficult but he needs to try.

Gustavo is my prof for E290 it's not available, so I picked E355 His lectures are boring and disproportionate He will often speak too much and rush to finish the lecture skipping over key details in the process. The TAs aren't much help as they barely respond to emails Marking is also based on luck, depends on the quantity of writing rather quality

Gustavo is my prof for E290 it's not available, so I picked E355 His lectures are boring and disproportionate He will often speak too much and rush to finish the lecture skipping over key details in the process. The TAs aren't much help as they barely respond to emails Marking is also based on luck, depends on the quantity of writing rather quality

Gustavo is someone who knows the material well, answers questions you have, and actually cares about how well you do. The exams correspond to what he teaches in class, and if your midterm grade is bad, it gets replaced by your final exam grade if that is higher. He is very kind and is not strict. I would recommend taking him for Econ courses.

Gustavo is someone who knows the material well, answers questions you have, and actually cares about how well you do. The exams correspond to what he teaches in class, and if your midterm grade is bad, it gets replaced by your final exam grade if that is higher. He is very kind and is not strict. I would recommend taking him for Econ courses.
He is a good professor, new to SFU.
He is a good professor, new to SFU.
She really cares about her students and encourages you to do well. Approachable.
Great professor. Very informative class sessions. Very organized content. Highly recommend her.

Dr. Nazir's lectures are full of interesting facts related to Economics development. She includes topics related to countries and case studies to explain application of concepts. Excellent presentations and helpful web resources make her a great instructor.  She is an asset for SFU.

Maliha is awful at lecturing and unhinged most of the time. She goes around the class asking students where they are from (very cringe!) If you are sitting in her lecture room, get ready to be pointed out by her. She tends to target certain students in class by asking questions. She definitely has her favorites, biased prof.
Great overall!

Great Prof Overall. 
Pro: Interesting lectures, lots of practice exams, easy to follow materials. 
Cons: Heavy Argentinian Accent (hard for International like me), VERY HEAVY WORKLOAD, lots of readings.
Good professor. We also had recorded lectures so could always refer back to them. Clear slides and explanation. Lots of written assignments to do, similar to Econ 220W.
Good prof!

He is really laid back for the most part, but he doesn't mess around when it comes to cheaters. If you show up to lecture and pay attention, you will do well on the exams. Expectations are fair for written assignments. Really easy to follow his content and he is available if you need extra help. Definitely one of the best lecturers at SFU.
Martin is a great prof. He makes the topic look easy and tries hard to make the class fun. He is also very knowledgeable
no empathy, marks are distributed like they blindfolded themselves and threw darts on a wall. avoid him. my nightmares include him and this lecture

Grading is a mess. Makes fun of you when you ask questions during class and doesn't give you helpful feedback. My friend wrote an essay 4 hrs before due and got 100% while another friend of mine worked on the essay for 2 weeks and got 70%. High discrimination. Do not take his classes. You will fail if you get 70% or less.

I understand why many students love him but he grades assignments and exams with a "pass/fail" mindset and because of that the curve of the course gives you a C when your overall average is 84%. I got a D because I got 71% and lost my financial help from the school. I contacted him about this but he didn't care. FIND ANOTHER PROF!

Absolutely my fav prof at sfu!!! Have taken 2 courses with him and both were great! He is just so chill and always delays the deadlines. Overall not hard for a 4-unit course. Just have to write a few papers and 2 exams. Talk to the TAs for revision for your paper and study the lecture notes for the exams and you will be good.

Professor Santamaria is quite good! The material was dry at parts, but he trys to make it more interesting. If you have a solid econ background I think you'll find Econ355W quite easy, but I got tripped up with some of the models. Good mix of assignments and he gives you practice midterms/finals that are accurate. Attending class makes it easier!

Exams are easy but lectures are tedious. Maybe 40% of the lecture material Will actually show up on the exam. For 355, just remember the basic diagrams for all models and the basic concepts discussed in class. The math that you deread will never be needed. There is too much math to remember anyway.

Econ355W is upper writing course but it comes easy if you take this profs class. 5 essays no more than 500 words each in entire term. Super easy exam, no formula derivation, no essay on exams, Just some simple math and model theory.

Great professor overall. Very easy to follow, explains things very well. Even when material is dry he finds a way to make it interesting. His exams are very straight forward, if you study and attend lectures you will get a good grade.

This was the one econ class that I was most looking forward to taking and I was utterly disappointed.  When he was actually interested, the prof seemed more interested in getting laughs than helping students learn.  Further, a quarter of the lectures were taken up by student presentations which is not what I expect my tuition money to go towards.

i think he dreaded the 3 hour lectures as much as we did. spoke in a monotone and read right off the slides so i stopped showing up after lecture 3. tests are fairly easy and fair though cuz i think the TA's did the marking. this class has potential to be so interesting and i think he killed it

Highly knowledgeable; potential to be an excellent lecturer.  However, he is extremely rude, abrasive, and intransigent.  A number of my classmates shared the same concerns; his demeanor and unpredictablilty with respect to mood and attitude do not create a healthy or encouraging environment in which to learn.

Akbar can be rude and mean sometimes. But he is a great prof. Very clear on what he is teaching. just go to the lecture every time, pay more attention on what he is saying, its a easy A. He gives very easy exams and always wants his students to do well in his class. He is helpful and nice during office hrs, too!
The greatest prof ever.
Nice guy, and a pretty easy class.  Easy to ace assignments, midterm was kind of hard but final was easier.  The prof overall has a good attitude.
Nice prof, hard TA. He sometimes repeat himself but he just want to make sure we understand the material. Fair midterm, harder final
Great! Ghosh is very nice and approachable. His lectures were clear and organized. Exams were very fair. Overall just great prof. Very recommended.
He's very nice
He interacts with the class quite often and is helpful during office hours.  Also, very approachable.

He is a really good prof. Always willing to help and actually cares about his students.  He explains really well in lectures.  If you attend lectures and keep up with the notes, you will definitely do well in his class. I highly recommend him.
First day of class, 156 students, 3rd week of class 46... you decide...
